questions.question: How does full translation differ from total translation?[1]
questions.solution_html:
• Related but distinct concepts in Catford's theory. Full translation - extent of the translation
  • process - every part of the Source Language (SL) text is subjected to translation -replaced by Target
  • Language (TL) material - focuses on the breadth of the text being translated. Total translation is a
  • technical term - involves the comprehensive replacement of SL text - specifically entails replacing SL
  • grammar and lexis with equivalent TL grammar and lexis - includes the consequential replacement of
  • SL phonology/graphology with non-equivalent TL phonology/graphology - delves into the specific
  • levels of language being addressed - highlighting that not all linguistic levels achieve equivalence,
  • especially phonological and graphological aspects.

questions.question: Explore the tension between foreignizing and domesticating translation. How do these approaches differ?
questions.solution_html:
• Foreignizing - a strategy where the translator deliberately retains the cultural and linguistic
  • characteristics of the source text in a way that the work feels foreign to the target audience -
  • authenticity and the uniqueness of the original work are preserved - at the risk of making the work
  • challenging or less accessible to the target audience – Domesticating - involves adapting the text to the
  • established norms and conventions of the target culture, making it look more familiar and acceptable to
  • the audience - prioritizes readability and accessibility but may sacrifice some of the nuances and
  • cultural richness of the original text. / {CO1}

questions.question: How do cultural differences influence translation, according to E.V Ramakrishnan ? [5x5 = 25] Part E Essay Type Questions Each Question carries 15 marks
questions.solution_html:
• Value or meaning of translation can only be ascertained with reference to the entire field of literary
  • production - translated text is constituted not only by the strategies of translation but also by the
  • dialectics between the economic and symbolic capital in the culture of the target language - For eg the
  • nature of addressivity in the fictional text of Khasak undergoes a complete change in translation -
  • Malayalam original uses a large number of speech genres which may be traced to the caste difference
  • in the lively subculture of a rural place - in its translation these dialects are rendered opaque and caste
  • differences are projected onto religious differences - Cultural differences in translation - Translation is
  • about culture and language together - some cultural words have no exact match - Translator must
  • explain or recreate the idea - “Transcreation” – keeping both meaning and feeling - Translation
  • becomes a bridge between two cultures. / {CO1}
